QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_38

question.text: Krishna Capital Cat II AIF realises INR 60 crore from the sale of a portfolio company in which it invested INR 25 crore. The fund's waterfall provides for 100% return of capital, 8% preferred return (cumulative INR 5 crore already hit via prior distributions), and 80/20 carry thereafter with a full GP catch-up. Focusing ONLY on THIS exit (assume capital fully returned via this exit and pref is met mid-way), what is the GP's INDICATIVE carry on this INR 60 crore if the incremental profit beyond capital + pref is INR 30 crore?

answer.text: INR 6 crore (20% of INR 30 crore incremental profit).

explanation.text: The Logic: Workbook pp.92-93, 114-115 and 125-126 support an incentive/performance fee on returns above the Preferred Return, with catch-up describing the manager's receipt of residual profits until the agreed share is reached. Under the stem's simplified arithmetic, GP carry = 20% x INR 30 crore incremental profit beyond capital and preferred return = INR 6 crore, matching keyed option A. The Trap: 40% (option B) would imply a 60/40 split, which is not the source's basis. 10% (option C) understates the carry rate. 25% of gross proceeds (option D) ignores return-of-capital and the preferred return entirely. Note: In a standard waterfall, carry is calculated on the profit slice ABOVE return of capital and preferred return — never on gross proceeds. Always strip capital and pref out before applying the carry rate.
